transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Well, doctor, it’s probably not a very big thing compared with what you usually hear, but… I’ve been getting a bit stuck checking things. Like boxes, lists, the drawers in our condo—I'll look, and then I find myself going back over them again before I can move on.

I know I’ve already checked. I do know that. But it’s hard to just leave it, and my wife is usually waiting for me to be done. I suppose that’s what finally made me think I should ask someone about it.
Do you find yourself having upsetting thoughts or mental images that come up unexpectedly and make you feel anxious, especially before you check things?

Yes… I suppose I do, though I wouldn’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is. It’s more like a nagging thought that pops up—like maybe I threw away something important from my old teaching files, or put a tool in the wrong box.

I’ll tell myself, “No, that’s probably not true,” but the thought sort of comes back around anyway, and then I have trouble settling until I check. Does that make sense?
When you have these nagging thoughts, do you feel you need to do something specific, like checking or counting, to make the anxiety go away or prevent something bad from happening?

Yes, I think so. Not counting, really, but checking. I don’t like to admit it, because it sounds a bit silly, but I’ll check the same boxes or lists or the drawers in our condo more than once before I can let it go.

I know perfectly well I already looked, and my wife is often waiting for me to just be done with it… but until I check again, I don’t quite feel settled enough to move on. Does that answer what you mean?
When you check these things again, do you feel like you’re trying to prevent something bad from happening, or is it more about just feeling uncomfortable until you check?

I think it’s more the uncomfortable feeling, really. I’m not usually thinking something terrible will happen, exactly… it’s just that if I don’t check the box or the list or the drawer again, I can’t quite move on.

I know I already looked, which is the frustrating part, and I know my wife is waiting for me to just leave it be. But I still feel I need to look once more before I can settle. Does that make sense?
Has this checking behavior caused you significant distress or started to interfere with your daily life, such as taking up a lot of time or affecting your work or relationships?

A little, yes… though I don’t want to overstate it. It’s not as if I’m unable to function, but unpacking the condo has taken far longer than it really should have, because I keep feeling I need to verify things before I can move on.

And I have put off some of my library tutoring preparation, and even hobbies I enjoy, because I get stuck thinking, “Just make sure this is right first.” It’s embarrassing to say, but it does slow me down. I suppose that counts as interfering, doesn’t it?
Do these checking behaviors take up a significant amount of your time each day—like more than an hour—or cause you a lot of distress even when you’re not doing them?

I’m not sure it’s more than an hour every single day, doctor… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But it does add up, especially with the condo. Unpacking has taken much longer than it really should because I keep feeling like I need to verify things are right before I can move on.

And I have been putting off my library tutoring preparation, and some hobbies too, because I get stuck on that “just check it enough first” feeling. It’s frustrating more than anything. I don’t know if that’s the level you mean, but it has been interfering some.
Have you noticed feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in activities you usually enjoy, even before this checking behavior started to bother you?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I have my off days like anyone my age, I suppose, but I haven’t really noticed being depressed or losing interest in things before this started bothering me.

If anything, I still want to do my usual things… I just sometimes get slowed down before I get to them. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you ever have thoughts that come into your mind that you don’t want or that bother you, and do you try to push them away or do something else to get rid of them?

Yes… I suppose I do, though I’m a little embarrassed to put it that way.

It’s usually these nagging thoughts, like maybe I threw away something important from my old teaching files, or put a tool I’ll need into the wrong box. And I’ll tell myself, “No, that’s probably not true,” but the thought comes back anyway. Then it’s hard to settle unless I do something to reassure myself.

Does that make sense? I don’t mean it’s constant, exactly, but it does bother me.
When you have these nagging or intrusive thoughts, do they feel completely involuntary—like they don’t belong to you or that you wish they would stop—and do you try to neutralize them by checking?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. They don’t feel like something I’m choosing to think about, exactly. It’s more that the thought pops back in — like, what if I threw away something important from my old teaching files, or what if a tool I’ll need is in the wrong box.

I can tell myself, “That’s probably not likely,” and I do know that logically. But it doesn’t always settle it. So then I’ll check, just to quiet it down. I don’t like admitting that, but yes, I suppose that is what happens.
When you check these things again, is it mainly to reduce the uncomfortable feeling or anxiety that comes with the thought, even though you know it’s probably not necessary?

Yes… I think that’s probably the main reason, if I’m being honest. It’s not that I truly believe I haven’t checked. I usually know perfectly well I already looked.

But then I’ll go back to the same boxes, or a list, or the condo drawers, just to make that uncomfortable feeling settle down enough so I can move on. My wife will be waiting for me to just leave it be, and I know she’s right… but I feel better for a bit after I check. I suppose that’s what you mean, isn’t it?
Are these intrusive thoughts and checking behaviors related to a fear of contamination or something else, like symmetry, harm, or making a mistake?

Not contamination, no… at least I don’t think so. It’s more about making a mistake, I suppose.

I get stuck on the thought that I may have thrown away something important from my old teaching files, or put a tool I’ll need in the wrong box. And even if I tell myself, “Well, that’s probably unlikely,” it comes back and I have trouble letting it go. It sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud, but that’s the sort of thing it is.

When you experience these intrusive thoughts about possibly making a mistake, do you feel driven to check things repeatedly in order to reduce the anxiety or discomfort, even though you know it’s probably unnecessary?

Yes… yes, I think so. I don’t mean to make it sound worse than it is, but that is really what brought me in.

I’ll check the same boxes, or the lists I’ve made, or drawers at the condo, and even though I know I’ve already looked, I feel like I can’t quite move on until I look again. My wife will be waiting for me to just leave it be, and I know she’s right. But checking seems to settle me down, at least for a little while. Does that make sense?

Have you ever had intrusive, unwanted thoughts that are disturbing to you—such as thoughts about causing harm to someone, or about sexual or religious topics—that make you feel anxious and that you try to neutralize by doing something else, like checking?

No, not really those kinds of thoughts… not about harming anyone, or sexual or religious things. At least, nothing like that that I can think of.

For me it’s more ordinary, I suppose, but it still gets under my skin. I’ll keep getting this nagging thought that I may have thrown away something important from my old teaching files, or put a tool I’ll need in the wrong box. And I can tell myself, “That’s probably not true,” but it comes back anyway and I have trouble settling until I’ve checked. Does that answer what you mean?
Do the intrusive thoughts about possibly making a mistake happen before the urge to check, and does checking help reduce the anxiety those thoughts cause, even just temporarily?

Yes… I think that’s the order of it. I’ll have the thought first, like, “What if I put that in the wrong box?” or “What if I missed something on the list?” And then I feel I ought to check.

It’s not that I don’t know I already looked—I do. But I’ll end up checking the same boxes, the lists, or drawers at the condo again before I can really move on. My wife will be waiting for me to leave it alone, and I know she’s right. Checking does calm me down a bit, at least for the moment. I hope that’s what you’re asking.
